'''DeMar Darnell DeRozan''' (born August 7, 1989) is an American professional [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[Sacramento Kings]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC Trojans]] and was selected ninth overall by the [[Toronto Raptors]] in the [[2009 NBA draft]]. Nicknamed "'''Deebo'''", DeRozan is a six-time [[NBA All-Star]] and a three-time [[All-NBA Team]] member. DeRozan is currently fourth among active NBA players on the [[List of NBA career scoring leaders|all-time scoring list]].

DeRozan spent nine seasons with the Raptors, where he became the franchise's [[List of NBA franchise career scoring leaders|all-time leading scorer]] and led the team to five playoff runs. He was traded to the [[San Antonio Spurs]] in the summer of 2018 and the [[Chicago Bulls]] in 2021. He was traded to the [[Sacramento Kings]] in the summer of 2024. DeRozan won a gold medal with the [[United States men's national basketball team|United States national team]] in the [[2014 FIBA Basketball World Cup|2014 World Cup]] and the [[Basketball at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2016 Summer Olympics]].

==Early life==
DeRozan was born on August 7, 1989 in [[Compton, California]] to Frank and Diane DeRozan. Frank died in 2021.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Spears |first1=Marc J. |title=From 'Big Dog' to Dejounte, DeMar DeRozan takes care of his family |url=https://andscape.com/features/from-big-dog-to-dejounte-demar-derozan-takes-care-of-his-family/ |website=Andscape |access-date=December 6, 2025 |date=February 21, 2022}}</ref>

==High school career==
DeRozan attended [[Compton High School]] and was ranked as one of the top college recruits in the nation from the class of 2008. He was ranked No. 3 in the nation by [[Rivals.com]] and No. 6 by Scout.com.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://scouthoops.scout.com/a.z?s=75&p=9&c=4&pid=88&yr=2008 |title=2008 Football Recruiting Prospects |website=Scouthoops.scout.com |access-date=August 21, 2016}}</ref> He played on the varsity basketball team for all four years of high school. As a freshman, he averaged 26.1 points and 8.4 rebounds. During his sophomore year, he averaged 22.6 points and 8.4 rebounds, while as a junior he averaged 22.3 points, 7.8 rebounds, 3.0 assists, and 3.2 steals.<ref name = "born"/>

As a senior averaging 29.2 points and 7.9 rebounds per game,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.usabasketball.com/men_team.php?bios%3Dderozan_demar |title=USA Basketball |access-date=September 2, 2008 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080616014425/http://www.usabasketball.com/men_team.php?bios=derozan_demar |archive-date=June 16, 2008 }}</ref> DeRozan led Compton High School to a 26–6 record, a second consecutive [[Moore League]] championship and the CIF Division IAA Southern Section quarter-finals. For his efforts he was awarded the Moore League [[Most Valuable Player]] Award and named to the California All-State team. DeRozan was a member of the 2008 [[McDonald's All-American Team]], and also won the 2008 McDonald's All-American Slam Dunk Competition.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.trojannyc.com/2008/03/demar-derozan-w.html |title=TrojanNYC: Demar DeRozan Wins McDonald's All-American Dunk Contest |access-date=September 4, 2008 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080930234347/http://www.trojannyc.com/2008/03/demar-derozan-w.html |archive-date=September 30, 2008 }}</ref> He was also invited to play in the 2008 Jordan Brand Classic at [[Madison Square Garden]] and the Nike Hoop Summit, where he scored a team-high 17 points.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://blog.newrecruitsports.com/?p%3D3 |title=Jordan Brand Classic 2008 | |access-date=September 2, 2008 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080928043546/http://blog.newrecruitsports.com/?p=3 |archive-date=September 28, 2008 }}</ref> DeRozan's achievements on the court in his senior year saw him earn first-team [[Parade All-America Boys Basketball Team|''Parade'' All-American]] honors and First Team Best in the West honors.<ref>{{cite web|last=Davis|first=Stacy|date=April 2, 2008|title=Parade All-American Boys Basketball Team|url=https://nychoops.rivals.com/news/parade-all-american-boys-basketball-team|website=NYC Hoops/Rivals.com|access-date=February 21, 2022}}</ref>

==College career==
[[File:2009-0319-NCAAs-004-DeMarDeRozan10.jpg|thumb|left|upright|DeRozan during a practice at the 2009 NCAA tournament]]
In November 2007, DeRozan signed a [[letter of intent]] to play basketball at [[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC]]. He chose USC over [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]] and [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Weinbach |first=Jon |url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB120485166974418241 |title=A Hot Prospect? |website=WSJ.com |date=March 7, 2008 |access-date=August 21, 2016}}</ref>

In his first game for the Trojans, DeRozan scored a team-high 21 points with seven rebounds in an exhibition game against [[Azusa Pacific Cougars|Azusa Pacific]], an 85–64 victory at the [[Galen Center]].<ref name=LAT110408>Gary Klein, [https://web.archive.org/web/20081108051217/http://www.latimes.com/sports/college/usc/la-spw-uschoops4-2008nov04,0,1963970.story DeMar DeRozan lifts USC in exhibition win], ''Los Angeles Times'', November 4, 2008, Accessed November 4, 2008.</ref> DeRozan had 14 points in his first career regular season game in a win over [[UC Irvine]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=283200030&campaign=rss&source=NCBHeadlines |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190120144150/http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=283200030&campaign=rss&source=NCBHeadlines |url-status=dead |archive-date=January 20, 2019 |title=UC Irvine vs. USC - Game Recap - November 15, 2008 - ESPN |website=[[ESPN]] |date=November 15, 2008 |access-date=August 21, 2016}}</ref> He scored 21 points along with a career-high 13 rebounds against UCLA in the Pac-10 Tournament semifinals, before scoring a career-high 22 points on 10-for-16 shooting to lead his team to a 61-49 win over Arizona State in the Pac-10 Tournament final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=290150030 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180620002253/http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=290150030 |url-status=dead |archive-date=June 20, 2018 |title=Arizona State vs. USC - Game Recap - January 15, 2009 - ESPN |website=[[ESPN]] |date=January 16, 2009 |access-date=August 21, 2016}}</ref> His efforts in the tournament saw him earn First Team Pac-10 All-Freshman honors in addition to being named Pac-10 Tournament MVP. The Trojans went to the [[2009 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament]] as a 10th seed, where they lost in the 2nd round to [[2008–09 Michigan State Spartans men's basketball team|Michigan State]].

DeRozan started all 35 season games for the Trojans, scoring in double figures 28 times and posting four double-doubles. He ranked third on team in points (13.9 ppg), second in rebounds (5.7 rpg), third in assists (1.5 apg), and second in field-goal percentage (.523, eighth-best in conference). DeRozan followed his regular-season efforts by averaging 19.8 points in USC's five postseason games. His 485 points ranks third all-time and his 201 rebounds is fourth all-time for a USC freshman.<ref name = "born"/>

==Professional career==
===Toronto Raptors (2009–2018)===
[[File:Demar derozan 2009.jpg|right|thumb|175px|DeRozan shooting over [[Jermaine O'Neal]] in a 2009 game]]

====Early years (2009–2013)====
On April 8, 2009, DeRozan announced his decision to enter the [[2009 NBA draft]] and forgo his final three years of eligibility at USC.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ocregister.com/articles/demar-derozan-usc-2358316-nba-draft |title=USC's DeRozan says he's entering NBA draft |website=Ocregister.com |access-date=August 21, 2016}}</ref> On June 25, 2009, he was selected ninth overall by the [[Toronto Raptors]] in the 2009 draft.<ref name=lupus>{{cite news|author=Doug Smith |url=https://www.thestar.com/sports/nba/article/657572 |title=DeRozan driven to improve mother's health | Toronto Star |newspaper=The Toronto Star |date=June 27, 2009 |access-date=August 21, 2016}}</ref> He stated that part of the reason he left for the NBA after only one year at USC was to help take better care of his mother, who has [[Systemic lupus erythematosus|lupus]].<ref name=lupus/>

On July 9, 2009, DeRozan signed his rookie scale contract with the Raptors.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/raptors/news/derozan_signs_070909.html |title=Raptors Sign First-Round Pick DeMar DeRozan | THE OFFICIAL SITE OF THE TORONTO RAPTORS |website=NBA.com |date=July 9, 2009 |access-date=August 21, 2016}}</ref> As the fourth contestant in the 2010 Sprite Slam Dunk Competition, DeRozan lost in the final round against three-time champion [[Nate Robinson]]. The final percentage was 51% to 49%. DeRozan was selected to compete for the 2011 Sprite Slam Dunk Competition as a replacement for injured guard [[Brandon Jennings]]. He finished in third place.

On December 31, 2010, DeRozan scored a then career-high 37 points against the [[Houston Rockets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/301231010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220501063208/https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/301231010|url-status=dead|archive-date=May 1, 2022|title=Rockets get ninth win in last 10 home games|website=ESPN.com|date=December 31, 2010|access-date=May 1, 2022}}</ref> He matched that career high two more times over the next three years—against the [[Utah Jazz]] on November 12, 2012, and against the [[Chicago Bulls]] on November 15, 2013.

====First All-Star appearance (2013–2015) ====
On January 22, 2014, DeRozan scored a then career-high 40 points against the Dallas Mavericks, shooting 15-of-22 from the field. On January 30, DeRozan was selected for the [[2014 NBA All-Star Game]] as a reserve guard for the Eastern Conference All-Star team. He finished the game with 8 points, 3 rebounds, and 2 assists in 15 minutes. On February 1, he recorded a 36 points and a career-high 12 assists in a loss to the Portland Trail Blazers. On March 28, he led the Raptors to a playoff berth for the first time since 2008, with a victory over the Boston Celtics. He scored 30 points in the win, along with 3 rebounds, 4 assists, and 1 steal. On April 13, he scored 30 points against the Detroit Pistons to lead the Raptors to tie a franchise record of 47 wins.

DeRozan's [[2013–14 NBA season|2013–14 season]] was a breakout year, averaging career-highs of 22.7 points, 4.3 rebounds, 4.0 assists, 30% from beyond the arc, and finished fourth in total free-throws made and seventh in attempts. He led the Raptors to a 48–34 record and a third-seed finish in the Eastern Conference.

In DeRozan's first playoff game against the [[Brooklyn Nets]] on April 19, 2014, DeRozan scored 14 points on a 3-of-13 shooting as the game resulted in a loss. In Game 2, DeRozan bounced back and scored 30 points on 9-of-21 shooting in a 100–95 win. On April 25, he recorded 30 points, 5 rebounds, and 5 assists in a loss. That 30-point game made DeRozan the first Raptor to score 30 points in back-to-back playoffs games, and the first Raptor to score 30 in multiple playoff games since [[Vince Carter]]. The Raptors went on to lose to the Nets in seven games.

In the Raptors' season opening game of the [[2014–15 NBA season|2014–15 season]] against the [[Atlanta Hawks]] in Toronto, DeRozan recorded career-highs with 11 rebounds and six steals, along with 15 points, in a 109–102 win.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20141029/ATLTOR/gameinfo.html |title=Hawks at Raptors - October 29, 2014 - Game Preview, Play by Play, Scores and Recap on |website=NBA.com |access-date=August 21, 2016}}</ref> On November 29, 2014, he was ruled out indefinitely with a torn left adductor longus tendon. ====First All-NBA selection (2016–2017)====
[[File:DeMar DeRozan Shooting Nov 2 2016.jpg|thumb|right|DeRozan shooting a jumpshot over [[Bradley Beal]] in 2016]]
On July 14, 2016, DeRozan re-signed with the Raptors to a five-year, $139 million contract.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/raptors/press-releases/derozan-071416|title=Raptors Re-Sign DeMar DeRozan|work=NBA.com|date=July 14, 2016|access-date=July 14, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Reina|first=Christopher|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/analysis/242550/Grading-The-Deal-DeMar-DeRozan-Stays-With-Toronto-On-$139M-Deal|title=Grading The Deal: DeMar DeRozan Stays With Toronto On $139M Deal|work=RealGM.com|date=July 1, 2016|access-date=July 14, 2016}}</ref> In the Raptors' season opener on October 26, 2016, DeRozan had his third career 40-point outing in a 109–91 win over the [[Detroit Pistons]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899382|title=DeRozan's 40 leads Raptors to 109-91 win over Pistons|work=ESPN.com|date=October 26, 2016|access-date=October 27, 2016}}</ref> Two days later, he had a 32-point effort in a 94–91 loss to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]]. DeRozan's combined 72 points bested [[Vince Carter]]'s franchise record of 65 for the most points through the first two games of a season, set in the 2003–04 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899429|title=Irving, James help Cavs hold off Raptors 94-91|work=ESPN.com|date=October 28, 2016|access-date=October 29, 2016}}</ref> With a 33-point effort on October 31 against the [[Denver Nuggets]], DeRozan became the first ever Raptor with three straight 30-point games to begin a season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899492|title=DeRozan, Lowry propel Raptors over Nuggets 105-102|work=ESPN.com|date=October 31, 2016|access-date=November 1, 2016}}</ref> With 40 points against the [[Washington Wizards]] on November 2, DeRozan tied [[Mike James (basketball, born 1975)|Mike James]]' franchise record with four consecutive 30-point games.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899505|title=DeRozan scores 40 points as Raptors keep Wizards winless|work=ESPN.com|date=November 2, 2016|access-date=November 3, 2016}}</ref> He passed that mark two days later, scoring 34 points in a 96–87 win over the [[Miami Heat]]. His five straight 30-point games set the best such start to a season since [[Michael Jordan]] did it for six straight games to open the 1986–87 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899521|title=DeRozan's 34 points push Raptors past Heat 96-87|work=ESPN.com|date=November 4, 2016|access-date=November 5, 2016}}</ref> On November 12, he scored 33 points against the [[New York Knicks]] for his eighth 30-point game in nine games, becoming only the fourth player to register 30-plus points in eight of the first nine games of a season, joining Michael Jordan, [[World B. Free]], and [[Tiny Archibald]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899581|title=DeRozan scores 33, Raptors beat Knicks 118-107|work=ESPN.com|date=November 12, 2016|access-date=November 13, 2016}}</ref> With 34 points against the [[Golden State Warriors]] on November 16, DeRozan became the first NBA player with nine 30-point games in his team's first 11 games since Jordan in 1987–88.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899615|title=Curry scores 35 points, Warriors top Raptors 127-121|work=ESPN.com|date=November 16, 2016|access-date=November 17, 2016}}</ref> DeRozan's six field goals against the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] on December 2 saw him pass [[Vince Carter]] (3,536) for second on the franchise's all-time list; [[Chris Bosh]] still led at the time with 3,614.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899726|title=Raptors beat Lakers 113-80|work=ESPN.com|date=December 2, 2016|access-date=December 3, 2016}}</ref> On December 28, he scored 29 points against Golden State and became Toronto's career scoring leader (10,290), passing Bosh's 10,275 points.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899927|title=Durant, Warriors deliver down stretch to hold off Raptors|work=ESPN.com|date=December 28, 2016|access-date=December 28, 2016}}</ref>

====Final year in Toronto (2017–2018)====
[[File:DeMar DeRozan (25716541587).jpg|thumb|DeRozan in 2018]]
On November 3, 2017, DeRozan scored 37 points in a 109–100 win over the [[Utah Jazz]], with 17 points and his third career four-point play coming in the third quarter.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400974879|title=DeRozan scores 37 as Raptors top Jazz 109-100 for 3-3 trip|work=ESPN.com|date=November 3, 2017|access-date=November 3, 2017}}</ref> On December 13, 2017, he matched his season high with 37 points in a 115–109 win over the [[Phoenix Suns]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975162|title=Demar DeRozan has 37 points, Raptors beat Suns 115-109|work=ESPN.com|date=December 13, 2017|access-date=December 14, 2017}}</ref> On December 21, 2017, he set a career high with 45 points in a 114–109 win over the [[Philadelphia 76ers]]. He also set a career high with six 3-pointers in nine attempts.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975218|title=DeRozan scores 45 points, Raptors rally to beat 76ers|work=ESPN.com|date=December 21, 2017|access-date=December 21, 2017}}</ref> On January 1, 2018, DeRozan scored a franchise-record 52 points to help the Raptors beat the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] 131–127 in overtime, matching the team record with their 12th consecutive home victory. DeRozan was the first player in NBA history to score 50+ points on New Years Day. He also became the third player in Raptors history to score 50 or more in a single game—the others being [[Vince Carter]] and [[Terrence Ross]], who each had 51.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975292|title=DeRozan scores franchise-high 52, Raptors beat Bucks 131-127|work=ESPN.com|date=January 1, 2018|access-date=January 1, 2018}}</ref> On January 8, 2018, he scored 35 points, including a go-ahead three-point play with 26.1 seconds left in overtime, to lift the Raptors to a 114–113 win over the [[Brooklyn Nets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975338|title=DeRozan helps Raptors beat Nets in OT after Lowry hurt|work=ESPN.com|date=January 8, 2018|access-date=January 8, 2018}}</ref> On January 13, 2018, he had a 42-point effort in a 127–125 loss to the [[Golden State Warriors]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975377|title=Curry returns with 24 points, Warriors beat Raptors 127-125|work=ESPN.com|date=January 13, 2018|access-date=January 14, 2018}}</ref> On January 18, 2018, DeRozan was chosen to as an NBA All-Star starter for the second consecutive season, marking his fourth overall selection to the game, leaving him third overall in franchise history behind Vince Carter and [[Chris Bosh]] at the time, both of whom had been selected on five occasions.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/raptors/press-releases/derozan-voted-starter-2018-nba-all-star-game|title=DeMar DeRozan Voted As Starter For 2018 NBA All-Star Game|work=NBA.com|date=January 18, 2018|access-date=February 3, 2018}}</ref> DeRozan joined Carter and [[Kyle Lowry]] as the only player with consecutive NBA All-Star Starter selections. DeRozan made 11 of 22 shots and matched his career high by making six 3-pointers to finish 6 for 10 from long range.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975515|title=DeRozan's shooting lifts Raptors over Blazers 130-105|work=ESPN.com|date=February 2, 2018|access-date=February 6, 2018}}</ref> On March 7, 2018, he scored 42 points in a 121–119 overtime win over the [[Detroit Pistons]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975712|title=DeRozan scores 42, VanVleet makes winning shot for Raptors|work=ESPN.com|date=March 7, 2018|access-date=March 8, 2018}}</ref>

In Game 2 of the Raptors' first-round playoff series against the [[Washington Wizards]], DeRozan matched his career playoff-high with 37 points, as Toronto took a 2–0 lead in a playoff series for the first time in franchise history with a 130–119 win. ===San Antonio Spurs (2018–2021)===
====First-round playoff exit (2018–2019)====
[[File:DeMar DeRozan Spurs (cropped).jpg|thumb|left|DeRozan with the Spurs in 2019]]
On July 18, 2018, DeRozan was traded, along with [[Jakob Pöltl|Jakob Poeltl]] and a protected 2019 first round draft pick, to the [[San Antonio Spurs]] in exchange for [[Kawhi Leonard]] and [[Danny Green (basketball)|Danny Green]].<ref name=trade>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/spurs-obtain-demar-derozan-jakob-poeltl-and-first-round-pick-raptors-exchange-kawhi-leonard-and|title=Spurs obtain DeMar DeRozan, Jakob Poeltl and first-round pick from Raptors in exchange for Kawhi Leonard and Danny Green|work=NBA.com|date=July 18, 2018|access-date=July 18, 2018}}</ref> The trade was controversial because DeRozan was a fan favorite in Toronto and had not been consulted about the trade by Raptors president [[Masai Ujiri]] beforehand; however, there was a perception that DeRozan was not a strong playoff performer, and trading away DeRozan's large contract freed up significant salary cap space.<ref>{{cite web | last=Campigotto | first=Jesse | title=What the Raptors can do now that the Giannis dream is over | website=CBC | date=2020-12-17 | url=https://www.cbc.ca/sports/the-buzzer-raptors-giannis-antetokounmpo-1.5846271 | access-date=2025-04-03}}</ref>

In his debut for the Spurs in their season opener on October 17, 2018, DeRozan had 28 points in a 112–108 win over the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401070699|title=DeRozan leads Spurs past Wolves 112-108; Butler scores 23|work=ESPN.com|date=October 17, 2018|access-date=October 17, 2018}}</ref> On October 22, he had 32 points and 14 assists in a 143–142 overtime win over the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401070729|title=Spurs rally to keep Lakers winless with LeBron, 143-142|work=ESPN.com|date=October 22, 2018|access-date=October 23, 2018}}</ref> On October 29, he had 34 points and nine assists in a 113–108 overtime win over the [[Dallas Mavericks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401070775|title=DeRozan outduels Doncic, Spurs' beat Mavs in OT 113-108|work=ESPN.com|date=October 29, 2018|access-date=October 29, 2018}}</ref> On November 3, he scored 26 points in a 109–95 win over the [[New Orleans Pelicans]], thus scoring at least 25 points in seven of the team's first eight games. The only other San Antonio player to do so was [[George Gervin]] in 1978–79.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401070811|title=DeRozan, Aldridge lead Spurs to 109-95 win over Pelicans|work=ESPN.com|date=November 3, 2018|access-date=November 3, 2018}}</ref> On December 2, he had a season-high 36 points in a 131–118 win over the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071023|title=DeRozan's season-high 36 help Spurs beat Blazers, 131-118|work=ESPN.com|date=December 2, 2018|access-date=December 3, 2018}}</ref> On December 7, he recorded 36 points and nine assists in a 133–120 win over the Lakers.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071056|title=DeRozan's 36 points fuels Spurs past Lakers 133-120|work=ESPN.com|date=December 7, 2018|access-date=December 8, 2018}}</ref> On January 3, he recorded his first career triple-double with 21 points, 14 rebounds and 11 assists in a 125–107 win over his former team, the [[Toronto Raptors]]. DeRozan also recorded his first double-double in a half.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071239|title=DeRozan has triple-double, Spurs win in Leonard's return|work=ESPN.com|date=January 3, 2019|access-date=January 4, 2019}}</ref> On February 22, he played his first game in Toronto in a Spurs uniform. He finished the game with 23 points, 4 rebounds and 8 assists.<ref>{{cite web|title=Leonard scores 25 points, Raptors beat DeRozan, Spurs|website=ESPN.com|publisher=|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071549|format=|access-date=2021-06-13|last=|date=2019-02-23|language=en|pages=|quote=}}</ref>

On April 16, 2019, during Game 2 of the first round of the playoffs, DeRozan scored 31 points in a 105–114 loss to the [[Denver Nuggets]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Nuggets erase 19-point deficit in 114-105 win over Spurs |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401126828 |access-date=May 25, 2022 |website=ESPN}}</ref> The Spurs would go on to lose the series in seven games. His old team the Raptors would go on to win the [[2019 NBA Finals]].

====Back-to-back postseason absences (2019–2021)====
On January 29, 2020, DeRozan scored a season-high 38 points, alongside five assists, in a 127–120 win over the [[Utah Jazz]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=DeRozan's season-high 38 points helps Spurs top Jazz 127-120 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0021900711 |access-date=May 25, 2022 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> On March 10, he logged a season-high 12 assists, along with 13 points, in a 119–109 win over the [[Dallas Mavericks]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Aldridge's return helps Spurs rally past Mavericks, 119-109 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0021900965 |access-date=May 25, 2022 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> After the NBA season was suspended in March due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], the Spurs were one of 22 teams invited to the [[2020 NBA Bubble|NBA Bubble]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=NBA Disney World rules: Details of how the bubble will work with league set to resume play in Orlando |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/nba-disney-world-rules-details-of-how-the-bubble-will-work-with-league-set-to-resume-play-in-orlando/ |access-date=May 25, 2022 |website=CBS Sports|date=July 30, 2020 }}</ref> However, after finishing with a record of 32–39, the team failed to qualify for the [[2020 NBA playoffs|playoffs]], marking the first time since [[2013 NBA playoffs|2013]] that DeRozan's team did not reach the postseason.<ref>{{Cite web |title=It's over: For first time in 23 seasons, Spurs miss playoffs |url=https://www.nba.com/news/ap-spurs-miss-playoffs-streak-ends |access-date=May 25, 2022 |website=NBA.com}}</ref>

On April 26, 2021, DeRozan scored a season-high 37 points, alongside ten assists, in a 146–143 overtime win over the [[Washington Wizards]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Spurs outlast Wizards in OT, end Washington's streak at 8 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022000919 |access-date=May 25, 2022 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> Four days later, he logged a career-high tying 14 assists in a 140–143 overtime loss to the [[Boston Celtics]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Celtics rally from 32-point deficit, top Spurs 143-140 in OT |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022000950 |access-date=May 25, 2022 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> Although they qualified for the newly implemented [[Play-in game|play-in tournament]], the Spurs suffered a 96–100 loss to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] on May 19, eliminating the team from playoff contention for the second straight season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Spurs Clinch Spot in 2021 NBA Play-in Tournament; Latest Western Conference Standings |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/10002620-spurs-clinch-spot-in-2021-nba-play-in-tournament-latest-western-conference-standings |access-date=May 25, 2022 |website=Bleacher Report}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Grizzlies end Spurs' season, advance to face Lakers |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0052000131 |access-date=May 25, 2022 |website=NBA.com}}</ref>

===Chicago Bulls (2021–2024)===
====Bounce-back and third All-NBA selection (2021–2022)====

On August 11, 2021, DeRozan signed with the [[Chicago Bulls]] on a three-year, $85 million contract in a [[sign-and-trade deal]]; the Bulls sent [[Thaddeus Young]], [[Al-Farouq Aminu]], a protected first-round draft pick, and two second-round draft picks to the Spurs in exchange.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-acquire-demar-derozan|title=Bulls Acquire DeMar DeRozan|work=NBA.com|date=August 11, 2021}}</ref> As his usual number 10 was retired by the Bulls in honor of [[Bob Love]], DeRozan switched to wear number 11.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/chicago/bulls/bulls-announce-jersey-numbers-demar-derozan-lonzo-ball-more|title=Bulls announce jersey numbers for new roster additions|date=August 20, 2021 }}</ref>

===Sacramento Kings (2024–2026)===
On July 8, 2024, DeRozan signed with the [[Sacramento Kings]] on a three-year, $74 million contract in a [[sign-and-trade deal]] that also involved one of his former teams, the [[San Antonio Spurs]], with [[Chris Duarte (basketball)|Chris Duarte]], [[RaiQuan Gray]] and draft considerations to going to Chicago and [[Harrison Barnes]] to San Antonio.<ref>{{cite web|title=Sacramento Kings Acquire DeMar DeRozan|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/sacramento-kings-acquire-demar-derozan|website=NBA.com|date=July 8, 2024|access-date=July 8, 2024}}</ref> 

On February 10, 2025, DeRozan scored a season-high 42 points, including a baseline floater with 2 seconds left in overtime to lead the Kings to a 129–128 win over the [[2024–25 Dallas Mavericks season|Dallas Mavericks]].<ref>{{cite web |title= DeRozan scores 42 points, including OT winner, as Kings edge depleted Mavericks 129-128 |url= https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401705328 |website=ESPN.com |access-date=February 11, 2025 |date= February 11, 2025}}</ref> On March 20, DeRozan scored 22 points in a 128–116 loss to the [[2024–25 Chicago Bulls season|Chicago Bulls]], becoming the 27th player to achieve 25,000 career points.<ref>{{cite web|title=DeMar DeRozan becomes 27th player in NBA history to score 25,000 career points|url=https://www.nba.com/news/derozan-25000-points|website=NBA.com|date=March 21, 2025|access-date=March 21, 2025}}</ref> On April 11, DeRozan moved past [[Reggie Miller]] into 25th place on the NBA All-Time Scoring List.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401705750|title=Clippers hold off Kings 101-100 to remain tied with Nuggets for No. 4 in tight Western Conference|date=April 12, 2025|website=ESPN.com}}</ref> DeRozan finished the season averaging 22.2 points per game and in the process became just the sixth player in NBA history ([[Kareem Abdul-Jabbar]], [[Karl Malone]], [[Kobe Bryant]], [[Dirk Nowitzki]], [[LeBron James]]) to average 20+ points per game in 12 or more straight seasons (minimum 60 games played per season).<ref>{{cite web|title=Kings' DeMar DeRozan's latest record gives him case as most underrated scorer in NBA history|url=https://www.sportingnews.com/us/nba/sacramento-kings/news/kings-demar-derozan-record-most-underrated-scorer-nba-history/8323c1df86da17a165d03a8a|website=Sporting News|last=Heyen|first=Billy|date=April 17, 2025|access-date=April 17, 2025}}</ref>

On January 14, 2026, DeRozan recorded 27 points, six rebounds and five assists in a 112–101 win over the [[2025–26 New York Knicks season|New York Knicks]]. He passed [[Kevin Garnett]] to move into 22nd place on the NBA’s all-time scoring list.<ref>{{cite web |title= DeRozan moves to 22nd on career scoring list as Kings beat Brown, Knicks 112-101 |url= https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401810431 |website=NBA.com |date=January 14, 2026 |access-date=January 14, 2026}}</ref> On February 26, DeRozan moved into 20th place on the NBA’s all-time scoring list, surpassing [[John Havlicek]] and [[Paul Pierce]] during a 130–121 win over the [[2025–26 Dallas Mavericks season|Dallas Mavericks]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Baer |first=Jack |title=DeMar DeRozan enters NBA's all-time scoring Top 20 |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/demar-derozan-enters-nba-time-031459186.html |website=Yahoo Sports |date=February 26, 2026 |access-date=February 26, 2026}}</ref> On March 15, DeRozan scored a season-high 41 points and recorded 11 assists to lead the Kings to a 116–111 victory over the [[2025–26 Utah Jazz season|Utah Jazz]]. ==National team career==
[[File:20140814 World Basketball Festival DeMar DeRozan cropped.jpg|thumb|left|upright|DeRozan with Team USA at the 2014 World Basketball Festival]]
DeRozan was a member of the [[United States men's national basketball team|United States national team]] that won the gold medal in the [[2014 United States FIBA Basketball World Cup team|2014 FIBA Basketball World Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/raptors/mackenzie_082314 |title=DeRozan Heading To World Cup With USA Basketball | Toronto Raptors |website=NBA.com |date=August 23, 2014 |access-date=August 21, 2016}}</ref> In nine games, he averaged 4.8 points, 1.0 rebounds and 1.2 assists per game.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fiba.basketball/basketballworldcup/2014/player/Demar-Darnell-Derozan |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180605151301/http://www.fiba.basketball/basketballworldcup/2014/player/Demar-Darnell-Derozan |url-status=live |archive-date=June 5, 2018 |title=DeMar DEROZAN (USA)'s profile - FIBA Basketball World Cup 2014 |website=FIBA.com |access-date=August 21, 2016}}</ref> He made a second appearance for Team USA at the [[Basketball at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2016 Summer Olympics]]. DeRozan averaged 6.6 points, 1.4 rebounds and 0.9 assists in seven games for Team USA in helping them win the Olympic gold medal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fiba.basketball/olympics/2016/player/Demar-Darnell-Derozan|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181120221405/http://www.fiba.basketball/olympics/2016/player/Demar-Darnell-Derozan|url-status=live|archive-date=November 20, 2018|title=DeMar DeRozan's Olympic profile|website=FIBA.com|access-date=September 22, 2016}}</ref>

==Personal life==
DeRozan is the son of Frank and Diane DeRozan.<ref name = "born">{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/draft2009/prospects/131.html |title=DRAFT 2009 Prospects - DeMar DeRozan |website=NBA.com |date=August 7, 1989 |access-date=August 21, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090922112520/http://www.nba.com/draft2009/prospects/131.html |archive-date=September 22, 2009 |url-status=dead }}</ref> DeRozan's mother was diagnosed with [[lupus]] when he was a small child. While with the Raptors, DeRozan helped raise awareness and educate Canadians on the disease in part by partnering with [[Lupus Canada]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.lupuscanada.org/q-demar-derozan/ |title=One-on-One with DeMar DeRozan |publisher=Lupus Canada |access-date=December 23, 2017 |archive-date=December 23, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171223102011/https://www.lupuscanada.org/q-demar-derozan/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> DeRozan lost his father Frank DeRozan on February 19, 2021 after battling several longtime health issues. He said he would regularly fly to Los Angeles from San Antonio or any city he was playing in to be by his side throughout his last moments.{{Citation needed|date=April 2025}}

DeRozan has a daughter born in 2013 named Diar, who gained national attention in 2023 after consistently shrieking during [[free throw]]s in the Bulls' [[NBA play-in tournament|play-in tournament]] game against the [[Toronto Raptors]]. The Raptors shot just 18-of-36 from the free throw line, with many calling Diar an integral piece of the Bulls' 109–105 victory.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/36173970/how-demar-derozan-daughter-diar-derozan-became-unsung-hero-bulls-play-victory|title=How DeMar DeRozan's daughter, Diar DeRozan, became the unsung hero of the Bulls' play-in victory|last=Collier|first=Jamal|date=2023-04-12|website=[[ESPN]]|language=en-US|access-date=2023-04-14}}</ref> After the game, Raptors forward [[Scottie Barnes]] admitted that the screaming had an impact on Toronto's free throw shooting.<ref>{{cite web | last=Brito | first=Christopher | title=DeMar DeRozan's daughter went viral when her screams helped the Bulls defeat the Raptors. Now, United is offering her a free flight to beat the Heat. | website=CBS News | date=2023-04-14 | url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/demar-derozan-daughter-diar-united-chicago-bulls-miami-heat/ | access-date=2025-12-14}}</ref> Diar later received several online threats.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cowley |first=Joe |date=2023-04-15 |title=DeMar DeRozan's daughter, Diar, got online threats during Bulls' victory in Toronto |url=https://chicago.suntimes.com/bulls/2023/4/14/23684216/report-diar-derozan-had-to-be-escorted-out-of-arena-in-toronto-demar-bulls-online-threats-security |access-date=2025-10-29 |website=Chicago Sun-Times |language=en-US}}</ref>

DeRozan has openly struggled with depression, and is an advocate for others suffering with it.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Smith|first1=Doug|title=Raptors' DeRozan hopes honest talk on depression helps others|url=https://www.thestar.com/sports/raptors/2018/02/25/raptors-derozan-hopes-honest-talk-on-depression-helps-others.html|access-date=May 21, 2018|publisher=Toronto Star|date=February 25, 2018}}</ref> After DeRozan and fellow NBA player [[Kevin Love]] spoke publicly on mental health it prompted the NBA to add a new rule that requires a team to have at least one full time licensed mental health professional on their staff.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mysanantonio.com/sports/spurs/article/DeRozan-continues-to-advocate-for-mental-health-14512066.php|title=DeRozan continues to advocate for mental health|last=Orsborn|first=Tom|date=2019-10-11|website=San Antonio Express-News|access-date=2019-10-15}}</ref> The duo also appeared in a PSA video by the NBA that launched the new mental health professional program alongside a new website with various mental health resources.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://andscape.com/features/demar-derozan-and-kevin-love-appear-in-psa-encouraging-people-to-seek-help-for-mental-health-issues/|title=DeMar DeRozan and Kevin Love appear in PSA encouraging people to seek help for mental health issues|last=Evans|first=Kelley D.|date=2018-05-02|website=[[Andscape]]|language=en-US|access-date=2019-10-15}}</ref> In 2024, DeRozan's book, ''Above the Noise: My Story of Chasing Calm'', was published by Harmony Books. The book describes his experiences with depression, growth, and the slow process of healing.<ref>{{Cite book |title=Above the Noise: MY Story of Chasing Calm |url=https://bookshop.org/p/books/above-the-noise-demar-derozan/20975021?ean=9780593581261 |access-date=November 19, 2024 |website=bookshop.org| date=September 10, 2024 | last1=Derozan | first1=Demar | publisher=Harmony/Rodale/Convergent | isbn=978-0-593-58126-1 }}</ref>

DeRozan is nicknamed "Deebo" after the character from the 1995 film ''[[Friday (1995 film)|Friday]]''. He received the name as a sixth grader when he beat up an eighth grader during a basketball game at school. DeRozan has reflected on the awareness of his neighborhood nickname: "When people call me that, you have to know me from back home, so when it started carrying over to the NBA, I was just like I don't know how it got to the league."<ref name="m407">{{Cite web |last=Beslic |first=Stephen |date=2023-05-18 |title=The story behind DeMar DeRozan's 'Deebo' nickname |url=https://www.si.com/nba/bulls/off-the-court/the-story-behind-demar-derozans-deebo-nickname |access-date=2025-03-03 |website=SI.com}}</ref>

DeRozan was mentioned in "[[Not Like Us]]", a [[diss track]] by the American rapper and fellow Compton native [[Kendrick Lamar]], amidst [[Drake–Kendrick Lamar feud|his highly publicized feud]] with the Canadian rapper [[Drake (musician)|Drake]] in May 2024. He was invited on stage during the 2024 [[The Pop Out: Ken & Friends]] concert held on [[Juneteenth]], where Lamar first performed "Not Like Us" live, along with fellow NBA player and Los Angeles area native [[Russell Westbrook]]. DeRozan additionally had a cameo in the music video of "Not Like Us", which was symbolically released on July 4, 2024. It won the 67th [[Grammy Award for Best Music Video]].

DeRozan got into an altercation with a fan at a [[sushi]] restaurant on April 19, 2025, after the fan shone the light from his phone in DeRozan's face.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ackerman |first=Sean |date=2025-04-19 |title=Breaking: DeMar DeRozan Involved in Public Altercation |url=https://www.si.com/nba/kings/sacramento-kings-news/breaking-demar-derozan-involved-in-public-altercation-01js85mbxbfk |access-date=2025-04-20 |website=Sacramento Kings On SI |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Anderson |first=Jason |date=2025-04-19 |title=Sacramento Kings star DeMar DeRozan caught on video in physical altercation |url=https://www.sacbee.com/sports/nba/sacramento-kings/article304598786.html |website=www.sacbee.com}}</ref>
